recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what the common denominator is and what the numerator becomes.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Combine over the common denominator
steps.margin_note: First mark. Neither piece has a limit as x → 2: each grows without bound in size, and the sign differs on the two sides. Combine them into one fraction first.
steps.memory_tip: x² − 4 already contains x − 2, so the common denominator is x² − 4 itself — nothing new has to be built.
lines: Neither part has a limit as x → 2 — each grows without bound in size — so the two are combined into one fraction.
x² − 4 = (x − 2)(x + 2), so the common denominator is (x − 2)(x + 2)

recall.must_convey: That x² − 4 = (x − 2)(x + 2) is the common denominator and the numerator becomes x + 2 − 4 = x − 2.
accept: take the common denominator x minus two into x plus two
the numerator becomes x plus two minus four which is x minus two
combine the two fractions into one first
x squared minus four already has x minus two in it

steps.why: The difference of two limits rule needs each limit to exist, and neither piece has a limit here. Combining first replaces the difference by a single fraction whose numerator and denominator are both zero at 2, which is a form the chapter can handle.
common_mistakes: Taking the limit of each piece separately and writing ∞ − ∞.
Writing the numerator as x + 2 + 4 by dropping the minus sign of the second fraction.

steps.label: Cancel (x − 2) and substitute
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Say x ≠ 2 before cancelling. What is left, 1/(x + 2), is defined at 2, so substitution finishes it.
steps.memory_tip: After combining, the whole numerator is x − 2 — the same factor as below — so the fraction reduces to 1/(x + 2).
lines: As x → 2 we have x ≠ 2, so (x − 2) may be cancelled:

recall.must_convey: That (x − 2) cancels leaving 1/(x + 2), and x = 2 gives 1/4.
accept: cancel x minus two and one over x plus two is left
put x equals two to get one by four
x minus two cancel chesi two substitute cheste one by four
one over two plus two is one by four

steps.why: A limit as x → 2 uses only values of x other than 2, so (x − 2) is not zero and may be divided out. The surviving expression 1/(x + 2) is defined at 2, so direct substitution is valid.
common_mistakes: Writing 0 above after cancelling and giving the answer as 0.

insider_note: Neither part has a limit on its own, so combine them over the common denominator FIRST. The top collapses to x − 2, which cancels and leaves 1/(x + 2).
